text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a modern software development practice where developers frequently merge their code changes into a shared main repository. The heart of CI is the automated build process. Every time a developer pushes new code, a CI pipeline automatically compiles the entire project and runs a series of tests. This means that problems, such as broken code or failing tests, are caught immediately, often within minutes of the change. This early detection is crucial because it prevents small issues from becoming large, time-consuming problems later. By making integration smoother and faster, CI encourages teams to work collaboratively and release software with greater confidence.
